Subject: Recap: Renewal discussion + proposed add-route pilot

Helena — thanks again for the call just now. Quick recap and asks so we can align with your procurement timeline.

Key items we covered:
- Renewal target: Oct 1 renewal effective date.
- Proposed expansion: add a new high-throughput route for conversational assistants (route B) that will sit alongside your existing route (route A).
- Estimated incremental volume: 600K–1.2M tokens/day in month 1 of the ramp (we discussed a 30–60 day ramp).
- Model mix: primary conversational model (~80% token usage), embeddings/utility routes (~20%).

Open asks for ClearPath:
1) Confirm the targeted blended $/1M tokens threshold you need to hit for procurement sign-off (you mentioned a target band).
2) Share any constraints on per-call latency or on-prem requirements.
3) Can procurement take a 30–60 day PO for a trial/step-up or do you need firm annual commitment upfront?

Attached is a simple 1M-token projection we put together from our call — it maps the ramp scenarios to projected monthly spend and blended $/1M for three tier options. If you can confirm which range (low/mid/high) best represents your budget, we’ll return a candidate blended pricing table and a step-up schedule for your legal/finance.

Next steps (proposed):
- Vanessa: send blended pricing options + step-up schedule (today).
- ClearPath: confirm budget band + procurement approach (reply here).
- Optional: 30-min follow-up with Marcus to validate tokenization and routing assumptions.

Thanks — talk soon.

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Budget band: for the renewal + expansion we are targeting $650–800 per 1M tokens (this is the combined blended target across routes). Our procurement threshold for formal approval is $700/1M or lower, ideally.
- Commitment: we can take a 90-day PO for the pilot/step-up if terms allow a conversion into a longer-term commitment afterwards. Procurement prefers staged commitments rather than an immediate annual lock.
- Model mix: estimate is roughly 78% conv/chat usage, 22% embeddings/semantic search. We expect short bursts of high RPS during business hours; latency SLO is 300ms p95 for the conv route.

Samir and procure are looped to confirm the PO process. We’ll try to give a firm signal on the budget band by Friday EOD.

Subject: Proposed pricing options & step-up paths (for procurement)

Helena / team — per our call and Helena's note on budget band, attached is a short pricing packet (PDF) with three candidate approaches. Summary below to make it easy for procure/finance:

Option A — Conservative step-up (lower near-term discount)
- Tiering: Month 1 baseline = existing renewal rate for route A; Month 2–3 step to blended discount of $730/1M; Month 4 onward re-evaluate (conversion to annual).
- Good for: teams that want limited near-term commitment and lower risk.

Option B — Aggressive step-up (recommended for targeted $700/1M)
- Tiering: 90-day pilot PO covers ramp to 1M tokens/day; blended target = $695/1M starting in month 2, with usage-based credits if ramp < 60%.
- Add-route mechanics: route B added as a canary at 10% traffic first, then expand. Automatic fallback to route A if latency/quality issues detected.

Option C — Volume-commit (best unit economics)
- 12-month committed volume with quarterly step-ups; blended target from $640–680/1M depending on guaranteed commitment band.
- Good for predictable high-volume workloads.

Unit economics notes (high level):
- Our baseline unit cost for the conv route (post-quantization and batching) is ~ $0.28–0.35/1k tokens of compute cost; network/infra adds marginally depending on region.
- Blended customer price reflects a mix of conv + small utility routes and includes operational SLA overhead and caching benefits.

Requested confirmation from ClearPath:
- Which option (A/B/C) should we formalize into an SOW/90-day PO?
- If Option B: confirm target blended $700/1M (Helena indicated $650–800 band; this gets us right in the middle).
- Any required attachment/license wording for the canary route?

I attached redwood-blend-pricing-v2.pdf with the line-item math and an example invoice. If you want Marcus to jump on a 20–30 min technical call to validate tokenization assumptions and route mapping we can do that tomorrow morning.

[Attachment: redwood-blend-pricing-v2.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk procurement through the mechanics.

Subject: Technical note: tokenization & routing impact on blended rate

Samir / Helena — quick technical addendum to the pricing packet to help your engineering/finance model expected tokens/call:

- Tokenization: based on your sample prompts, median tokens per conv call ~ 1.1k (prompt + response); peak session flows push ~2.4k tokens. Embeddings average ~180 tokens per request.
- Route mix impact: if 78% of tokens are conv, the blended effective $/1M will skew towards the conv route's unit price; small changes in avg tokens/call change monthly spend notably.
- Batching & cache: enabling prefix caching for recurring prompts reduces billable tokens by an estimated 7–12% (dependent on prompt repeatability).
- Measurement ask: please share a 72-hour sample traffic dump (CSV or gz) with columns: unix_ts, route_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, user_id (anonymized ok). With that we can simulate a tight blended price and show invoice-level projections.

If procurement needs a conservative bind, Option A is easiest. If you want to hit $700/1M in the pilot, we can tighten model selection, enable aggressive batching, and run a short pre-canary test to validate the 90-day PO terms.

—
Marcus Lin
